interval.scope: Opt-in terrain, material-emission and lighting submissions on the shared device. Enable before warmup to observe incoming work. Work submitted before capture is enabled, ore/feature/vine jobs, copies, driver compilation and untimestamped work are not covered. Host sequence marks classify whole submissions; device timestamps use a separate clock. Boundary-crossing and aborted submissions are excluded from pass aggregates. Pending work is not awaited. Union removes overlapping pass timestamps, not host time. Neither gaps, pass sums nor unions are an idle/utilization percentage. Zero passes can mean unavailable timestamps. Dropped records make coverage incomplete. Peaks count tracked submissions, not hardware occupancy.

preservation.scope: Same process, closed/reopened world definition; outside measured generation

decision: Retain for correct bounded opt-in interval attribution, not a generation-speed claim. All timing confidence intervals include no change. No meaningful timing difference established under shared-host variation. Existing lifetime ABI unchanged; disabled path is one atomic check per recorded submission with no capture allocation/lock.
notes: All four benchmark comparisons have five trials per variant in ABBA order.
The shorter default-off Metal comparison is nominally -4.36%; the longer one is -1.14%. Neither resolves a performance difference; CPU default-off is nominally -0.75%.
Capture-on versus capture-off is nominally +0.64% throughput; not a speedup claim.
Host load fluctuated; five-sample bootstrap intervals are descriptive and wide, not proof of exact zero overhead.
Preliminary artifacts named without final- were superseded by explicit aborted-versus-completed observation semantics and are excluded from retained statistics.
